blocks.text: Draft for Jared's approval. Built only from the monthly MLS® figures (SnapStats) for condos and townhomes in New Horizons. No local notes, sold prices, building list or live listing feed yet; see the open items.

blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal. The reports count condos and townhomes together in one line, so this table cannot separate the two. Shares are this community’s count divided by the Coquitlam total for condos and townhomes that month.

blocks.text: Listings of condos and townhomes in New Horizons fell from 33 in June to 24 in October (−27.3%), and 35 sold across the 5 months. In October the community held 3.1% of Coquitlam’s 779 condos and townhomes listed.
Condos and townhomes or houses in New Horizons?
New Horizons also had 5 houses listed and 2 sold in October, against 24 condos and townhomes listed. The New Horizons houses page has those figures.

blocks.text: New Horizons Condos and Townhomes: streets and boundaries

items.t: New Horizons is a small house pocket in east-central Coquitlam whose centre streets are Nestor Street, Harwood Avenue, Toba Drive and Sechelt Drive, with Mariner Way as the through road at its west side; the City publishes no boundary for this board sub-area name, so treat street names, not a map line, as the check.
The pocket's addressed anchor is École Nestor Elementary at 1266 Nestor Street, the School District No. 43 (Coquitlam) school physically inside the street pattern the houses and attached homes front.
Mariner Way separates this pocket from the Ranch Park streets to the south-west, and the same Mariner Way corridor carries the buses that serve both pockets.

blocks.text: New Horizons Condos and Townhomes: the housing stock

items.t: That distinction matters for a buyer on this page: attached homes added under the small-scale rules are strata or rental units created lot by lot on Nestor Street, Harwood Avenue and Toba Drive lots, not homes in a named strata complex with a single depreciation report.

blocks.text: New Horizons Condos and Townhomes: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: The pocket's school is a French-language-named district school: the Ministry's school list records it as École Nestor Elementary, kindergarten to Grade 5, at 1266 Nestor Street — a detail a buyer only sees on the district or Ministry listing, not on the street sign.

Integrated stormwater management applies to small-scale residential projects in Coquitlam, to manage runoff from roofs and driveways and protect local creeks — relevant to any New Horizons lot adding hard surface in a multi-unit conversion.

The City classifies its creeks for environmental value and monitors flow, level and water quality on various creeks, so a lot draining toward a local creek corridor carries a monitoring and setback context even where no development permit area is mapped on the lot itself.

blocks.text: New Horizons Condos and Townhomes: getting around

items.t: Route 152, Coquitlam Central Station to Lougheed Station, runs Mariner Way at the pocket's west side via Dewdney Trunk Road, with some trips via Chilko Drive, then continues via Hickey Drive and Austin Avenue.

blocks.text: New Horizons Condos and Townhomes: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check the City's floodplain mapping work, which covers the Coquitlam, Fraser and Pitt river floodplains, against the specific lot rather than the neighbourhood name before purchase.

blocks.text: New Horizons home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

59 condos sold in New Horizons with a median price of $695,000 (the middle half sold between $640,000 and $776,400), taking a median of 20 days to sell at 97.4% of the last list price; 3% sold above list. They had a median $761 per square foot, a median year built of 2016 and a median strata fee of $441 a month. 5 townhomes sold in New Horizons with a median price of $1,055,000, taking a median of 37 days to sell at 96.9% of the last list price; 0% sold above list. They had a median $666 per square foot, a median year built of 2010 and a median strata fee of $370 a month.

items.t: New Horizons, Coquitlam Homes for Sale

faq.q: How many condos and townhomes are for sale in New Horizons?
faq.a: At the end of October 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 24 condos and townhomes listed in New Horizons. That is a month-end count and it moves daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.

faq.q: Is New Horizons a buyers’ or sellers’ market for condos and townhomes?
faq.a: In October 2026, condos and townhomes in New Horizons had a sales ratio of 33%, which the reports’ scale reads as a sellers’ market. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.

faq.q: How many condos and townhomes sold in New Horizons from June to October 2026?
faq.a: 35 condos and townhomes sold in New Horizons over those 5 months, out of 596 in all of Coquitlam.

faq.q: Do these numbers separate condos from townhomes?
faq.a: No. The monthly reports publish condos and townhomes as one line, so every count here includes both. Jared can pull the split for a specific building or street.

faq.q: Which elementary school is actually inside New Horizons?
faq.a: École Nestor Elementary, at 1266 Nestor Street, is the School District No. 43 school inside the pocket, listed for kindergarten to Grade 5.

faq.q: Can a New Horizons house lot be turned into several attached homes?
faq.a: A multi-unit conversion also needs the City's fire flow form filed with the building permit application, confirming water supply for the lot.

faq.q: Which library branch serves this pocket?
faq.a: Coquitlam Public Library runs two branches, and the City Centre Branch at 1169 Pinetree Way is the branch on the City Centre side of the city that this pocket's Mariner Way buses run toward; the other branch is Poirier at 575 Poirier Street. Branch programs and hours are the library's own listings, so check them there rather than assuming a neighbourhood branch exists.
